original_question: Describe Finsler metrics on S^2 of flag curvature 1.
target_in_paper: Problem 8.5.1 in §8.5 (“Finsler metrics with positive flag curvature”): describe Finsler metrics on S^2 of flag curvature 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation: it identifies the correct manifold (the 2-sphere S^2), the correct geometric objects (Finsler metrics), and the exact curvature normalization (flag curvature 1). In fact, it is essentially the wording of Problem 8.5.1 itself. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, it helps to say explicitly that the flag curvature is constant and identically equal to 1 everywhere, not merely positive. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

The problem is global on S^2, not just local and not restricted to special subclasses such as projectively flat metrics; the paper notes that the projectively flat constant-flag-curvature-1 metrics on S^2 are already described, so the open problem is the full description beyond that subclass. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

The intended scope includes irreversible as well as reversible Finsler metrics; the paper immediately notes that the reversible case is already settled (it must be the round Riemannian metric), so the unresolved content is mainly in the nonreversible case. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

The target is the classification/description of the metrics themselves, not merely a description of possible geodesic-flow behavior; the paper says the latter is understood even though the metrics are not fully classified. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

If one wants a fully formal stand-alone statement, one may say ‘globally defined Finsler metric on S^2’ or use the standard smooth/classical meaning of ‘Finsler metric’; the survey problem itself does not impose a sharper regularity class in its wording. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

No ambient ring/field, polynomial degree, homogeneity restriction, nilpotency condition, or asymptotic quantifier such as ‘for all sufficiently large m’ is part of this paper’s formulation; those categories are not applicable here. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
refined_question: Give a complete global description of all Finsler metrics F on the 2-sphere S^2, without assuming reversibility, whose flag curvature is constant and identically equal to 1. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
justification: The draft is almost verbatim the paper’s own Problem 8.5.1, so it clearly targets that statement rather than a broader neighboring issue. The surrounding discussion fixes the intended scope: reversible examples are already known to be the round metric, projectively flat examples on S^2 with constant flag curvature 1 are already classified, Bryant constructed non-projectively-flat examples, and yet the full classification remains open. Section 2.2 is relevant nearby context because the Katok examples on S^2 are recalled there and are cited again in §8.5 as examples with constant flag curvature 1. This shows that the paper’s intent is the global classification problem for all such Finsler metrics on S^2, especially beyond the already understood special families. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
